blocks.text: A strain gauge rosette glued to the skin of a pressure vessel gives three numbers, and from them you must work out the largest strain and the direction in which it acts. Mohr's circle turns the algebra of stress and strain transformation into a picture in which the answer can be read off a circle.

blocks.markdown: At a point under **plane stress** the state is given by $\sigma_x$, $\sigma_y$ and $\tau_{xy}$ on an element aligned with $x$ and $y$. On an element rotated by $\theta$ the normal and shear stresses are different, yet they are all found on a single circle. For each plane, plot its normal stress $\sigma$ on the horizontal axis and its shear stress $\tau$ on the vertical axis (with the shear axis pointing **downward**, so that a counterclockwise rotation of the element appears as a counterclockwise rotation on the circle). The collection of all planes is a circle.

blocks.title: Mohr's circle for plane stress
blocks.text: The circle has centre $C=\left(\dfrac{\sigma_x+\sigma_y}{2},\,0\right)$ and radius $R=\sqrt{\left(\dfrac{\sigma_x-\sigma_y}{2}\right)^2+\tau_{xy}^2}$. The points $X=(\sigma_x,\tau_{xy})$ and $Y=(\sigma_y,-\tau_{xy})$ represent the faces of the original element, and they lie at opposite ends of a diameter.

blocks.caption: Principal stresses are where the circle crosses the $\sigma$ axis ($\tau=0$); the maximum in-plane shear stress equals the radius and acts on planes with normal stress $C$.

blocks.title: Principal and maximum shear stresses
blocks.prompt: A point is in plane stress with sigma_x = 80 MPa, sigma_y = -40 MPa and tau_xy = 30 MPa. Construct Mohr's circle and read the principal stresses, the maximum in-plane shear stress and the principal angle.

steps.text: Principal stresses are where the circle meets the horizontal axis.
Maximum in-plane shear equals the radius and acts on planes with normal stress equal to C.
The line from C to X makes 2 theta_p with the sigma axis; tan 2 theta_p = 30/60.

blocks.answer: sigma_1 = 87.1 MPa and sigma_2 = -47.1 MPa with the sigma_1 plane 13.3 degrees counterclockwise from the x-axis; tau_max = 67.1 MPa.

blocks.markdown: **Points on the circle are planes in the material.** Rotating the element physically by an angle $\theta$ moves the corresponding point round the circle by $2\theta$, in the **same sense** (clockwise or anticlockwise) as the physical rotation. Planes $90^\circ$ apart in the material are $180^\circ$ apart on the circle, which is why the faces $X$ and $Y$ are at opposite ends of a diameter, and why the planes of maximum shear are $45^\circ$ from the principal planes ($90^\circ$ on the circle).

blocks.title: Stress on an inclined plane
blocks.prompt: For the same stress state, find the normal and shear stress on a plane whose normal is rotated 30 degrees counterclockwise from the x-axis.

steps.text: On the circle, the point moves through 2 theta = 60 degrees. Equivalent analytic formulas are:
Substitute with the standard convention (tau_xy positive when it acts in the +y direction on the +x face).
Check: the point lies on the circle.

blocks.answer: On the 30 degree plane the normal stress is 76.0 MPa and the shear stress is -37.0 MPa (negative: it acts opposite to the positive sense on that face).

blocks.caption: Strain transformation is identical if tau is replaced by gamma/2

blocks.markdown: **Strain rosettes.** A strain gauge measures only the normal strain along its own direction. To find the full strain state we use three gauges, for example a 45-degree rosette at $0^\circ$ ($a$), $45^\circ$ ($b$) and $90^\circ$ ($c$). From the transformation $\varepsilon_\theta=\varepsilon_x\cos^2\theta+\varepsilon_y\sin^2\theta+\gamma_{xy}\sin\theta\cos\theta$ it follows that $\varepsilon_x=\varepsilon_a$, $\varepsilon_y=\varepsilon_c$ and $\gamma_{xy}=2\varepsilon_b-\varepsilon_a-\varepsilon_c$.

blocks.title: Rosette analysis
blocks.prompt: A 45-degree rosette gives readings epsilon_a = 800, epsilon_b = 500 and epsilon_c = -200 microstrain (gauges at 0, 45 and 90 degrees to x). Find gamma_xy, the principal strains, and the strain in a direction 30 degrees from x.

steps.text: Mohr's circle for strain: centre and radius, using gamma/2 = 200.
Strain at 30 degrees from the transformation equation.

blocks.answer: gamma_xy = 400 microstrain, principal strains 838.5 and -238.5 microstrain, and the strain along the 30 degree direction is 723 microstrain.

blocks.title: Sign conventions and doubled angles
blocks.text: Always state the shear-stress sign convention you plot with. Angles on the circle are twice the physical angles and rotate in the same direction. Strain uses gamma/2 on the vertical axis, so do not mix up gamma with gamma/2 when finding the radius.

points: Mohr's circle for plane stress has centre (sigma_x + sigma_y)/2 and radius sqrt(((sigma_x - sigma_y)/2)^2 + tau_xy^2); principal stresses are C plus or minus R and tau_max = R.

Points on the circle are planes in the body: a physical rotation theta corresponds to 2 theta on the circle in the same sense, so principal and maximum-shear planes are 45 degrees apart in the material.
Strain transformation is identical with gamma/2 in place of tau; a 0-45-90 rosette gives epsilon_x = epsilon_a, epsilon_y = epsilon_c and gamma_xy = 2 epsilon_b - epsilon_a - epsilon_c.

questions.stem: On Mohr's circle for plane stress, the centre lies at which normal stress?

options.text: The larger of sigma_x and sigma_y

distractorRationale.a: Correct: the centre is at the average normal stress.
distractorRationale.b: This is half the difference, a component of the radius.
distractorRationale.c: tau_xy is a vertical coordinate, not the centre.
distractorRationale.d: The extremes sit at the ends of the diameter, not at the centre.

questions.explanation: The circle is symmetric about the mean of sigma_x and sigma_y, so the centre has coordinates ((sigma_x + sigma_y)/2, 0).

questions.stem: An element is physically rotated by 20 degrees. How far, and in which sense, does the corresponding point move on Mohr's circle?

distractorRationale.a: Angles on the circle are twice the physical angle.
distractorRationale.b: Same sense is retained by the construction.
distractorRationale.d: Correct: angles double on the circle and rotate the same way.

questions.explanation: Because stress components depend on cos 2 theta and sin 2 theta, the circle angle is 2 theta. The rotation sense is the same as the physical rotation.

questions.stem: What does the radius of Mohr's circle represent?

distractorRationale.a: sigma_1 equals C + R, not R.
distractorRationale.d: That difference is twice a leg of the radius triangle.

questions.explanation: Because the lesson plots tau downward (clockwise-positive convention), the highest point on the page is (C, -R) and the lowest is (C, +R); either way R is the largest shear stress magnitude: R = (sigma_1 - sigma_2)/2.

questions.stem: A 45-degree strain rosette has gauges at 0 (a), 45 (b) and 90 (c) degrees to the x-axis. Which expression gives the shear strain gamma_xy?

distractorRationale.a: Ignores epsilon_c and the factor of two.
distractorRationale.c: Correct: from the transformation at 45 degrees.
distractorRationale.d: This is twice the radius component, not gamma_xy.

questions.explanation: At 45 degrees epsilon_b = (epsilon_a + epsilon_c)/2 + gamma_xy/2, so gamma_xy = 2 epsilon_b - epsilon_a - epsilon_c.

questions.stem: True or false: on a principal plane the shear stress is zero, so principal planes correspond to the points where Mohr's circle crosses the normal stress axis.
questions.explanation: Principal stresses are by definition the normal stresses on planes with zero shear. These are the intersections of the circle with the horizontal axis.

questions.stem: A point in plane stress has sigma_x = 60 MPa, sigma_y = -20 MPa and tau_xy = 30 MPa. Using Mohr's circle, find the larger principal stress in MPa.
questions.explanation: Centre = 20 MPa and radius = sqrt(40^2 + 30^2) = 50 MPa, so sigma_1 = 20 + 50 = 70 MPa.

questions.stem: At a point, sigma_x = 120 MPa, sigma_y = 40 MPa and tau_xy = -50 MPa (standard convention). Find the angle theta_p from the x-axis to the plane of the larger principal stress, positive counterclockwise, in degrees.
questions.explanation: tan 2 theta_p = 2(-50)/(120 - 40) = -1.25 so 2 theta_p = -51.3 degrees and theta_p = -25.7 degrees (clockwise). This is the plane of sigma_1 = 80 + 64.0 = 144.0 MPa, which a check with the transformation equation confirms.

questions.stem: A 0-45-90 rosette (a at 0, b at 45, c at 90 degrees to x) reads epsilon_a = 600, epsilon_b = -100 and epsilon_c = -300 microstrain. Find the normal strain in a direction 60 degrees counterclockwise from the x-axis, in microstrain.
Describe how to construct Mohr's circle for a plane-stress state and how to read the principal stresses, the maximum in-plane shear stress and the orientation of the principal planes.
markingGuide: Plots X = (sigma_x, tau_xy) and Y = (sigma_y, -tau_xy) with a stated sign convention
Draws a circle on the diameter XY, centre (sigma_x + sigma_y)/2
Principal stresses are where the circle crosses the sigma axis: C plus or minus R
Maximum in-plane shear equals the radius R, at normal stress C
Angle from CX to the sigma axis is 2 theta_p, so theta_p is half of it, in the same sense
questions.explanation: The circle encodes the transformation equations. Reading intersections and the radius gives the extreme values without algebra.

questions.stem: Explain why angles on Mohr's circle are twice the physical angles, and use this to explain why the planes of maximum shear stress are at 45 degrees to the principal planes and carry a normal stress equal to the average of the principal stresses.
markingGuide: Transformation equations contain cos 2 theta and sin 2 theta, so the point moves by 2 theta
Same rotation sense as the physical rotation
Planes 90 degrees apart in the body are 180 degrees apart on the circle
Principal planes are on the sigma axis and maximum shear is at the top or bottom of the circle, 90 degrees away on the circle
Therefore 45 degrees in the body, and the normal stress there equals the centre value (sigma_1 + sigma_2)/2
questions.explanation: The geometry of the circle says that the top point is a quarter turn from the principal points. Halving angles gives 45 degrees in the material, and the top point's abscissa is the centre.
